easy.def: A Hawaiian party with food, music and dancing.
examples: We went to a luau.
The luau had hula dancers.
A luau is a party.

more.def: A party in Hawaii with a big feast, music and dancing.
examples: We ate roast pork and fruit at the luau.
Hula dancers performed at the luau.
The luau was held on the beach at sunset.

easy.def: Good things that happen by chance.
examples: Good luck on your test!
It was luck that we found it.
I have bad luck today.

more.def: Things that happen by chance, good or bad, which you do not control.
examples: It was pure luck that we found the key in the grass.
Good luck with your science project!
With a little luck, the rain will stop before the game.

easy.def: By good luck.
examples: Luckily, it did not rain.
Luckily, I had an umbrella.
Luckily, no one was hurt.

more.def: In a way that is fortunate, by good luck.
examples: Luckily, I had an umbrella with me.
Luckily, the glass did not break.
Luckily, the bus was still there.

easy.def: Having good things happen to you.
examples: I was lucky to find a coin.
This is my lucky hat.
You are lucky to have a big yard.

more.def: Having good things happen by chance.
examples: We were lucky that the rain stopped just before the game.
He felt lucky to have such kind grandparents.
It was a lucky guess, but it was right.

easy.def: Bags and suitcases that you take on a trip.
examples: We packed our luggage.
The luggage is heavy.
Carry the luggage.

more.def: The bags and suitcases that you take with you when you travel.
examples: We checked our luggage at the airport.
The luggage was piled by the door.
He carried the heavy luggage up the stairs.

easy.def: A short quiet time in the middle of noise or activity.
examples: There was a lull in the storm.
A lull in the talk.
The lull was short.

more.def: A short period of calm or quiet in the middle of something busy or noisy.
examples: There was a lull in the storm, and we ran to the car.
During a lull in the game, we ate snacks.
A lull in the conversation let me ask my question.

easy.def: To make someone calm or sleepy.
examples: The song lulled the baby.
The rain lulled me to sleep.
A lullaby lulls a child.

more.def: To calm someone or make them sleepy with a soft, gentle sound or movement.
examples: The soft music lulled the baby to sleep.
The sound of rain on the roof lulled me.
The gentle rocking lulled the kitten.

easy.def: A soft song to help a baby sleep.
examples: Mom sang a lullaby.
The lullaby was sweet.
The baby loved the lullaby.

more.def: A soft, gentle song that is sung to help a baby or a child go to sleep.
examples: Mom sang a lullaby, and the baby fell asleep.
Grandma hummed a lullaby from her childhood.
The soft lullaby made me feel sleepy.

easy.def: Wood that is cut into boards.
examples: We bought lumber for the fence.
The lumber is in a pile.
Dad cut the lumber.

more.def: Wood from trees that has been cut into boards and beams for building.
examples: Trucks carried lumber from the sawmill to the building site.
Dad bought lumber to build a shed in the yard.
The pile of lumber smelled of fresh pine.

easy.def: To walk slowly and heavily.
examples: The bear lumbered along.
An elephant lumbers by.
The big truck lumbered up the hill.

more.def: To move slowly and heavily, with big, clumsy steps.
examples: The bear lumbered out of the cave after its long winter sleep.
The old truck lumbered up the steep hill.
An elephant lumbered across the dusty plain.

easy.def: A person who cuts down trees for wood.
examples: The lumberjack chopped a tree.
A lumberjack wears boots.
The lumberjack has an axe.

more.def: A person whose job is to cut down trees and prepare them for lumber.
examples: The lumberjack cut down a tall pine.
A lumberjack wears sturdy boots and a warm shirt.
The lumberjacks floated logs down the river.

easy.def: Giving off light.
examples: The moon is luminous.
A luminous star.
The clock face is luminous.

more.def: Giving off a bright or glowing light.
examples: The luminous moon lit up the dark field.
A luminous star twinkled over the roof.
The clock's face was luminous, so we could read it in the dark.

easy.def: A small, hard piece or bump.
examples: A lump of clay.
I felt a lump.
There is a lump in the bed.

more.def: A small, solid piece of something with no shape, or a bump.
examples: She rolled the lump of clay into a ball.
I put a lump of sugar in my tea.
There was a lump under the blanket.

easy.def: Full of lumps.
examples: The gravy was lumpy.
A lumpy bed.
The oatmeal is lumpy.

more.def: Full of small, hard lumps, or not smooth.
examples: The gravy was lumpy because the flour had not been stirred well.
The old mattress was lumpy and uncomfortable.
We walked across the lumpy ground.

easy.def: Having to do with the moon.
examples: A lunar eclipse.
The lunar surface.
A lunar landing.

more.def: Having to do with the moon.
examples: We watched a lunar eclipse, when the Earth's shadow covers the moon.
The astronauts took a lunar rock back to Earth.
A lunar month is about twenty-nine days.

easy.def: The meal you eat in the middle of the day.
examples: I eat lunch at noon.
My lunch is in my bag.
We have lunch at school.

more.def: The meal that people eat in the middle of the day.
examples: We ate lunch on the grass in the park.
She packed a sandwich and fruit for lunch.
The bell rang for lunch.

easy.def: A lunch, especially a fancy one.
examples: We went to a luncheon.
The luncheon was fancy.
She hosted a luncheon.

more.def: A lunch, especially a formal meal with guests.
examples: We went to a luncheon for the new mayor.
The luncheon was held at noon in a nice hall.
Grandma hosted a luncheon for her friends.

easy.def: The time of day when you eat lunch.
examples: It is lunchtime.
We play at lunchtime.
Lunchtime is at noon.

more.def: The time in the middle of the day when people usually eat lunch.
examples: At lunchtime, the whole school filled the cafeteria.
The bell rang for lunchtime.
We play outside at lunchtime if the weather is nice.

easy.def: A body part that you use to breathe.
examples: I breathe with my lungs.
Your lungs fill with air.
The lungs are in your chest.

more.def: One of two soft parts in your chest that fill with air when you breathe.
examples: You breathe air into your lungs.
The lungs fill up like balloons.
Running makes your lungs work hard.

easy.def: To move forward suddenly.
examples: The dog will lunge for the ball.
She lunged to catch it.
He lunged forward.

more.def: To make a sudden move forward.
examples: The goalie lunged to catch the ball.
The dog lunged at the stick.
She lunged forward to stop the vase from falling.

easy.def: A sudden move forward.
examples: He made a lunge for the ball.
The lunge was quick.
The cat made a lunge.

more.def: A quick movement forward.
examples: The cat made a lunge for the toy.
He made a lunge to catch the falling cup.
The goalie's lunge saved the game.

easy.def: To move with a sudden jerk.
examples: The bus lurched.
The boat lurched.
I lurched forward.

more.def: To make a sudden, jerky movement, or to stagger.
examples: The bus lurched forward and everyone swayed.
The boat lurched in the waves.
He lurched across the room in the dark.

easy.def: To attract someone to something.
examples: The smell lured the dog.
The bait lured the fish.
The music lured us in.

more.def: To attract or tempt someone to go somewhere or do something.
examples: The smell of pizza lured us into the shop.
The bait lured the fish to the hook.
The music lured the children closer.

easy.def: A fake bait used to catch fish.
examples: The fish took the lure.
I tied a lure to the line.
The lure shines.

more.def: A fake bait that is used to attract fish or other animals.
examples: The fish took the shiny lure.
I tied a lure to my fishing line.
The lure looked like a small insect.

easy.def: To hide and wait quietly.
examples: A cat lurked behind the door.
Frogs lurk in the pond.
Something lurks under the bed.

more.def: To stay hidden and quiet, often while waiting to jump out or watching what is going on.
examples: The crocodile lurked beneath the muddy water, waiting for a thirsty zebra.
My cat lurked behind the sofa until I walked past.
Shadows seemed to lurk in the corners of the old attic.

easy.def: Thick and green with healthy plants.
examples: The garden is lush.
The lush grass was soft.
We saw a lush forest.

more.def: Full of thick, healthy plants that grow well.
examples: The garden was lush after the spring rains.
We walked through a lush green forest.
Cows grazed in the lush grass of the valley.

easy.def: Very fancy and comfortable.
examples: The hotel was luxurious.
The luxurious bed was soft.
The robe was soft and luxurious.

more.def: Very comfortable and fancy, and costing a lot.
examples: The luxurious hotel had a pool and a big bed.
She wrapped herself in a luxurious soft robe.
The king rode in a luxurious carriage.

easy.def: Something very nice that you do not need.
examples: A pool is a luxury.
The hotel was a luxury.
A nap is a luxury.

more.def: Something that is very comfortable or expensive and that is not necessary.
examples: A swimming pool is a luxury.
The hotel was full of luxury.
A long, quiet bath is a luxury.
